title: installConsole
responsibility: Installs the console into a host or restores a file an install replaced, and renders what changed.

inputs.name: installConsole.flags
inputs.description: Options for installing into the SvelteKit project at host, which is resolved to an absolute path: policy and policyExport name the host's own module under $lib and the export it must provide, and base is one route segment such as /harness. data is the output directory of harness history build, which is bundled into the server unless bucket is set; bucket names a private bucket binding that holds the history instead, and prefix (which needs bucket) is the folder inside it. update and keep choose what happens to files holding other content, but may not both be set.

inputs.name: consoleObjects.data
inputs.description: The output directory of harness history build that holds the index, resolved against the current directory; it must contain index.json or the call rejects. Only the index's own files are listed from it, and the directory is read but never changed.

inputs.name: consoleObjects.prefix
inputs.description: The folder inside the bucket that the object keys are placed under; an empty value puts them at the bucket root. A non-empty value must start with a letter or digit and use only letters, digits, '.', '_', '/' and '-', and a trailing slash is dropped.

inputs.name: uninstallConsole.flags
inputs.description: host is the SvelteKit project directory to remove the console from, resolved to an absolute path. update removes generated files the host edited and keep leaves them in place as the host's own, and setting both throws before anything is removed.

inputs.name: renderConsoleUninstall.result
inputs.description: The uninstall result to render: the host, the files removed, put back and kept as the host's own, the changes this run recorded, and clean, which is true only when no record is left because nothing of the host was ever changed. The paths are relative to the host.

inputs.name: restoreConsoleFile.host
inputs.description: The project directory that holds the file and its harness.console.json record, resolved to an absolute path before it is read. The call rejects when the record has no change with a saved copy for the path.

inputs.name: restoreConsoleFile.path
inputs.description: The path, relative to the host, of a file an install replaced; the bytes saved before its most recent recorded change are written back. After the restore the file counts as the host's own again, so later installs leave it in place unless update is given.

inputs.name: renderConsoleChange.change
inputs.description: One recorded change to render: the file, its action (replaced, removed or restored), its reason, the time it was made, and the identities of the content before and after it, with the saved copy it can be restored from. The after identity is null when the file was removed.

inputs.name: renderConsoleInstall.result
inputs.description: The install result to render: the absolute host, the base, the policy as module#export, the files written, removed, kept as the host's own and replaced, the history measured or bundled, where the history is read from, and any warnings. The paths are relative to the host.

outputs.name: installConsole
outputs.description: Resolves once the console files are written and the record is updated, with the absolute host, the base and policy installed, the files written, removed, kept and replaced, the history measured from data (null without data), its storage, the bundled size (null when nothing is bundled) and any warnings about the host. A failed check, such as an invalid policy or files that would be overwritten without update or keep, rejects before any file is written.

outputs.name: consoleObjects
outputs.description: Resolves with one entry per object a private bucket must hold for the index, in path order: key is the object name, with the prefix and the file's index path unchanged, and file is the absolute path it is uploaded from. Only index.json, activity.json, revisions/ and sides/ files named by 40 hex characters and media/ files named by 64 hex characters with an extension are listed.

outputs.name: uninstallConsole
outputs.description: Resolves once the console is removed and the record is updated or deleted, with the host, the files removed, put back and kept as the host's own, the changes made in this run, and clean, which is true when the record was deleted because nothing of the host was ever changed.

outputs.name: renderConsoleUninstall
outputs.description: The text printed after an uninstall: a line naming the host and the number of files removed, a line for each file put back or kept, a line for each removed change, and a last line saying whether the record was deleted or still keeps the changes.
examples:
Removed the console from /srv/site: 4 files.
Nothing of the host was ever changed, so harness.console.json was removed as well.

Removed the console from /srv/site: 1 files.
  removed src/routes/harness/[...view]/+server.ts (edited since it was installed): 3b8d1a6f0c4e -> nothing, previous contents in .harness/console/replaced/3b8d1a6f0c4e9725d1b7a3f8e6c0d4a2b9f5e1c7d3a8b6f2e0c4d9a7b5f1e3c8
harness.console.json keeps the record of what was changed.

outputs.name: restoreConsoleFile
outputs.description: Resolves with the restored change for the path, which is also appended to harness.console.json: before is the content in place when the restore ran, after is the restored content, and the saved copy of the before content stays under .harness/console/replaced.

outputs.name: renderConsoleChange
outputs.description: The two lines printed for one change: the record file it was added to, then the action, path, reason, the first 12 hex characters of the content before and after (nothing when the file was removed), and the saved copy of the content before.
examples:
Recorded in harness.console.json:
  replaced src/routes/harness/+server.ts (host-owned): 5c1e0f7a9d2b -> a4f7c2e9d0b6, previous contents in .harness/console/replaced/5c1e0f7a9d2b4e68f3a1c0d7b9e2f4a6c8d0e1b3f5a7c9e2d4b6f8a0c1e3d5b7

Recorded in harness.console.json:
  restored src/routes/harness/+server.ts (restores what was replaced at 2026-11-15T10:42:17.318Z): a4f7c2e9d0b6 -> 5c1e0f7a9d2b, previous contents in .harness/console/replaced/a4f7c2e9d0b6814f3e5a7c2d9b0f4e6a1c8d3b5f7e9a2c4d6b8f0e1a3c5d7b9f

outputs.name: renderConsoleInstall
outputs.description: The text printed after an install: the base and host, the policy that decides every request, the history line (the bucket it is read from, the size bundled, or that nothing was bundled), the counts of files written and removed, a line for each kept file, the changed files under a review note, and a line for each warning.
examples:
Installed the console at /harness in /srv/site.
Every page, data and media request is decided by $lib/server/harnessPolicy#harnessPolicy.
Bundled 1 revisions and 1 media files as server-only modules, 0.54 MiB compressed.
Wrote 9 files, removed 0; they are listed in harness.console.json.

Installed the console at /harness in /srv/site.
Every page, data and media request is decided by $lib/server/harnessPolicy#harnessPolicy.
History is read from the private bucket bound as HARNESS_HISTORY under history/; nothing is bundled. Upload the index directory there with its paths unchanged (1 revisions, 1 media files).
Wrote 5 files, removed 4; they are listed in harness.console.json.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: Raised by the deliberate checks of installing, listing objects, uninstalling and restoring, with a message that says what to change. The promise-returning functions reject with it, and the update-with-keep check in uninstallConsole throws it synchronously.
